question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to the integral $\int_C 3y\cos{\left(x\right)}\,\mathrm{d}s$, where $C$ is the section of the curve $y=4e^{x}$ for $1\le x\le 2$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that the given curve is of the form $y=y(x).$ Therefore, by setting $x=t,$ we have $y=y(t)=4e^{t}.$ This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=\langle t,4e^{t}\rangle,\quad 1\le t\le 2
$$

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}j\\&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4e^{t})j\\&=i+(4e^{t})j\\\|r'(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2}\\&=\sqrt{1^2+(4e^{t})^2}\\&=\sqrt{16e^{2t}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=3y\cos{\left(x\right)}$, we obtain

$$
f(r(t))=3(4e^{t})\cos{\left(t\right)}=12e^{t}\cos{\left(t\right)}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{1}^{2}f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t\\&=\int_{1}^{2}(12e^{t}\cos{\left(t\right)})\cdot (\sqrt{16e^{2t}+1})\,\mathrm{d}t\\&=\int_{1}^{2}12\sqrt{16e^{2t}+1}e^{t}\cos{\left(t\right)}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the given curve is of the form $y=y(x).$ Therefore, by setting $x=t,$ we have $y=y(t)=t^{3}+3t.$ This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=\langle t,t^{3}+3t\rangle,\quad 1\le t\le 3
$$

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}j\\&=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t^{3}+3t)j\\&=i+(3t^{2}+3)j\\\|r'(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2}\\&=\sqrt{1^2+(3t^{2}+3)^2}\\&=\sqrt{\left(3t^{2}+3\right)^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=\frac{y^{2}}{x}$, we obtain

$$
f(r(t))=\frac{(t^{3}+3t)^{2}}{t}=t\left(t^{2}+3\right)^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{1}^{3}f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t\\&=\int_{1}^{3}(t\left(t^{2}+3\right)^{2})\cdot (\sqrt{\left(3t^{2}+3\right)^{2}+1})\,\mathrm{d}t\\&=\int_{1}^{3}t\left(t^{2}+3\right)^{2}\sqrt{9\left(t^{2}+1\right)^{2}+1}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
